label: sweep w4: 4 stage-A workers, 8 arms, wave 1 of 6
notes: Desktop parallelism sweep, training side. Every wave advances the same eight warm-started arms by 1196032 transitions, so wall clock per wave is the throughput comparison. **The worker order ascends and that is mandatory:** ensure_workers(target) iterates range(target) and never reaps a slot >= target, a worker only self-exits after 300s idle, and the gap between waves is one 30s poll -- so a wave after a higher-worker wave would inherit live extras that claim its queue work and measure more workers than its label. Waves 5 and 6 repeat at 12 to give wave-to-wave repeatability, which is what says whether a gap between neighbours is real. Arms resume from p2h-ep8-seed8 at 255213568 because a cold arm has short episodes, cheap stage A, and would understate the worker count needed.
